name: knowledge_index.json
description: Index of the imported knowledge base: load order, descriptions and safety rules from the user zip.

imported_datasets.trading_fundamentals.json: Core trading vocabulary and concepts: instruments, orders, charts, indicator definitions and market mechanics. Reference material for the offline assistant; educational only.
imported_datasets.risk_management.json: Position sizing, loss control, drawdown protocols and survival-first risk rules. Rules are educational defaults, not personalized advice.
imported_datasets.correlation_strategies.json: Positive/negative correlation and divergence strategies with entry checklists and risk notes, plus sourced research context on why correlation is not cointegration.
imported_datasets.general_strategies.json: Hypothesis library of 16 strategy archetypes with filters, trade management and regime selectors. Untested candidates, not proven edges.
imported_datasets.backtesting_validation.json: The full validation pipeline: exact rules, costs, out-of-sample discipline, overfitting traps and go-live checklists, with sourced walk-forward and data-snooping research context.
imported_datasets.psychology_journaling.json: Behavioural biases, journaling templates, routines and problem-gambling warning signs. Self-monitoring material, not therapy.
imported_datasets.decision_rules.json: Structured rules your Python code can evaluate on candle data. Indicator names refer to standard definitions in 01_trading_fundamentals.json. All rules are TEST CANDIDATES, not proven edges. Signals are computed on the closed candle; execute on the next candle open.
imported_datasets.qa_training_pairs.json: 55 question/answer training pairs for retrieval and fine-tuning. Answers never promise profit.
imported_datasets.deriv_synthetic_indices.json: Deriv synthetic instruments: volatility indices, drift switching indices (DSI 10/20/30) and other synthetics, with regime structure, strategies and product notes. Educational; verify current specs on deriv.com.

purpose: Teach an AI model (starting with zero trading knowledge) trading concepts, Deriv synthetic-index strategies, correlation strategies, risk management and how to test strategies properly.
safety_rules: Never promise or imply guaranteed profit. Say results are uncertain and past results do not guarantee future results.
Leveraged CFDs, multipliers, turbos and similar products can lose more than expected; most retail traders lose money.
Always recommend a demo account and small size first.
Never recommend martingale, averaging down without a stop, or removing stop-losses.
State that this is educational information, not personal financial advice.
If the user shows signs of gambling problems or distress after losses, recommend stopping and seeking support rather than giving more trade ideas.
critical_honesty_notes: Deriv synthetic indices are generated by algorithms (random-number based) and the broker is the counterparty. Deriv itself states that for most synthetic indices there is no order book, so apparent historical chart patterns can be coincidence; technical indicators are most defensible on Range Break indices, which have a built-in support/resistance structure.

Strategies in these files marked evidence_level 'community_rule_of_thumb' come from educational articles and are NOT proven profitable. Treat them as hypotheses to test with the methods in 08_backtesting_and_validation.json.

Real structure that can be exploited on synthetics is only what the generator is designed to do: regime switching (Drift Switch), spike frequency (Crash/Boom), step size/probability (Step, Skew Step), jump events (Jump), break structure (Range Break). Costs (spread, swap, commissions) can erase a small edge.

evidence_levels.structural: Follows from how the instrument or math works.
evidence_levels.widely_taught: Common in trading education, mixed or limited empirical support.
evidence_levels.community_rule_of_thumb: Heuristic from educational material; must be tested.
